title: The 4-Precondition Agent-Ready Ops Readiness Spec
subtitle: For 11-100 employee service businesses about to spend $20k+ on AI. Run this before you sign anything, or you'll be the 80% that ships a black box and blames the model.

sections.title: STRUCTURED INPUT DATA ,  Can an agent actually read your intake?
sections.description: If your intake collects free-text garbage and half the fields are optional, the agent breaks on day one. Fix the pipeline before you fix the AI.

items.text: Open your client intake form and count how many fields are free-text vs. structured (dropdowns, dates, enums)
items.tip: If more than 40% are free-text, rebuild it in Typeform or Tally before you touch any AI tool

items.text: List every place your team stores client knowledge (Notion, Drive, Slack, email, CRM, that one spreadsheet on Karen's laptop)
items.tip: If the number is higher than 3, your AI will only see one source and hallucinate the rest. Consolidate into 1-2 structured sources first

items.text: Mark every intake field as required or genuinely optional, then enforce it at the form level
Write down your file and folder naming convention, then check 10 recent client folders for compliance
items.tip: Inconsistent names are why your RAG returns the wrong document 30% of the time

items.text: Identify the last time each knowledge source was updated and who owns it
items.tip: Stale data is worse than no data. An agent will quote your 2023 pricing with full confidence

sections.title: DOCUMENTABLE DECISION LOGIC ,  Can your best person explain how they decide?
sections.description: If the answer is 'I just know,' you can't encode it. Tacit knowledge has to become explicit rules before any agent can replicate it.

items.text: Sit down with your top closer and have them write the exact criteria they use to qualify a lead
items.tip: If two partners give you two different answers, that's the work. Do it now, not after you've paid for the build

items.text: List the 10 most common edge cases your ops team handles weekly that aren't in any SOP
items.tip: This is where 80% of the real work lives. The happy path is the easy 20%

items.text: Map one repeating decision (pricing, scoping, triage) as an if/then tree with no more than 7 branches
items.tip: Use Whimsical or a Notion toggle list. If you can't get it under 7 branches, your scope is too wide

items.text: Document who currently fixes things when the process breaks and what they do
Flag every step in the workflow that requires human judgment vs. pattern matching
items.tip: Pattern matching = agent. Judgment = human-in-the-loop. Be honest about which is which

sections.title: NARROW INITIAL SCOPE ,  Did you pick one workflow, or are you boiling the ocean?
sections.description: Agents that try to handle every edge case on day one break on edge case #3. Start with the 80% of predictable cases and route the rest.

items.text: Pick ONE workflow to automate first, with a clear start trigger and a clear end state
items.tip: If you can't describe the trigger and end state in one sentence each, the scope is still too wide

items.text: Write down how many times per week this workflow runs and how long each run takes a human
items.tip: Under 5 runs/week or under 30 min/run and you probably shouldn't build it. The 90-Day Payback Rule won't clear

items.text: Estimate what % of runs follow the happy path vs. need exception handling
items.tip: If the happy path is under 60%, narrow the scope further before building

items.text: Define what 'this isn't working' looks like with a specific metric and timeline
items.tip: Example: 'If error rate is above 15% after 4 weeks, we kill it.' No kill criteria, no project

sections.title: HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP DESIGN ,  Did you design the review layer on day one?
sections.description: Every agent I've shipped routes about 15-20% of cases to human review. That's not failure, that's the design working. Build it in from the start.

items.text: Define the confidence threshold or condition that routes a case to human review
items.tip: In ClickUp or Slack, a 'needs review' queue with the agent's reasoning attached. Reviewer should decide in under 90 seconds

items.text: Name the actual person who will review flagged cases and how much weekly time they're allocated
items.tip: Unowned review queues become a graveyard. Budget 2-4 hours/week of a real human's time

items.text: Build a way for the reviewer's corrections to feed back into the system prompt or rule set
items.tip: Otherwise you fix the same mistake 40 times. A simple Supabase log + weekly prompt revision works

items.text: Make sure every agent decision is logged with input, output, and reasoning
items.tip: n8n execution logs or a Supabase audit table. When something goes wrong at 2am, you need the trace

items.text: Document how you turn the agent off and revert to manual in under 10 minutes

completion_cta.headline: Want me to score your top 3 gaps against the 90-Day Payback Rule?
completion_cta.description: Reply with your results and I'll send back which precondition to fix first, what it'll cost in hours, and whether the build clears payback inside 90 days. No deck, no discovery call, just the math.
